message.content: {"caption":"Diagram comparing a manually engineered traditional generalist-agent system with Alita’s minimal, self-evolving design.","description":"The diagram has two horizontal sections separated by a dashed line. In the upper section, a blue rounded box labeled “Traditional Generalist Agents” sits beside a central “Manager Agent” shown inside a cloud. Colored two-way arrows connect the manager to six surrounding agents: “Url Text Extractor” at upper left, “Image Captioner” above, “Relevant Patch Zoomer” at upper right, “Web Agent” at left, “Other Agents” at right, and “Path Generalist Classifier” and “Youtube Caption Crawler” below. To their right, a gears-and-hand icon accompanies “Large-scale Manual Engineering”; a gray arrow points right to a blue box listing “Incomplete Coverage,” “Limited Creativity & Flexibility,” and “Mismatch.” In the lower section, a yellow box labeled “Alita (Ours)” sits beside a “Web Agent,” connected by a two-way blue arrow to a cloud containing the “Manager Agent.” A rightward gray arrow leads from the manager to a “MCP Creation” block, then a rightward arrow leads to an icon labeled “MCP Box.” Below, a purple left-pointing arrow labeled “Self Evolving” runs from the MCP Box back toward the manager. To the right, “Minimal Predefinition” is paired with a green downward arrow and gear icon; “Maximal Self-Evolution” is paired with a red upward arrow and an icon of a person-like figure with sparkles. A gray arrow points right from this area to a yellow box listing “Scalable Dynamic Capability,” “Enhanced Creativity & Flexibility,” and “Cross-ecosystem Compatibility.”","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
